description: Hot kernels across isogeny-labs/crypto, isogeny-labs/cryptanalysis and lfd-summation-systems, with how each counts operations. Compiled by reading sources at crypto origin/main (sparse checkout), cryptanalysis 5dfcf82e6 and lfd-summation-systems 2cb270c. 'emitted' = the code already reports a count; 'derivable' = the count follows from shapes or inputs; 'none' = no count exists, itself a finding. Entries with status other than 'measured here' were NOT run; their measure commands are templates to be checked against the binary's actual output before use.

ops_counter.what: RhoResult.steps (walk steps) plus look_ahead_adds, table_adds, restart_adds; a step is one affine addition with a batched-inversion share, not one modmuladd

kernels.note: Counts walk steps, not field multiplications. Either convert with the documented multiplications per step and say so, or add a field-multiplication counter; until then an attainment against modmuladd_p62 is a lower bound by the per-step multiplication count.

ops_counter.what: walk_steps, group_additions, scalar_multiplications in the fixture's JSON; no count of GF(2^m) word operations or carry-less multiplies

kernels.measure: tools/optlevel/run.sh measure --ops-regex '"walk_steps":(\d+)' --op-class xor_u64 --out R.json -- env RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 target/release/examples/koblitz_rho_fixture 53 0 signed_frobenius 4 strong
kernels.note: Binary-field arithmetic is carry-less multiplication (PCLMULQDQ), for which v1 has no operation class. Finding: add a clmul_u64 class and a per-step clmul count before scoring this kernel.

kernels.path: src/cryptanalysis/ecbench/ (rho, BSGS, kangaroo and IC arms)

ops_counter.what: the ecbench counted unit (group-addition equivalents) and, where the curve counts them, fmul/fsqr/finv per arm

kernels.measure: run the arm under a frozen ecbench spec; take fmul from the session record and pass it with --ops
kernels.note: The counted unit is method-level and priced under AGENTS.md section 5a. Use the fmul counter, never GAE, as the operation: GAE mixes classes.

ops_counter.what: base_muls, descent_muls and their sub-counters, adds, base_steps
no operation counter found in the module (relations and trials only at the caller)

kernels.note: Finding: relation collection reports relations and trials but not the field or word operations they cost.

ops_counter.what: field_multiplications, field_ops, root_field_multiplications per run

kernels.note: Check the prime width of the run against the class (p31 or p62).

ops_counter.what: muladds (row-reduction multiply-adds)
Closure.muladds (the unit f4_fp_tower reports) and rows_reduced; also returned on censored runs

kernels.note: Sparse row reduction: declare the traffic from the echelon's entry count, or measure it on a PMU host; in-cache only for small closures.

ops_counter.what: word_ops (64-bit word xors) and pivots

kernels.note: The cleanest CPU case: the counter is exactly the class.

ops_counter.what: reduce_word_ops, criterion_word_ops, zero_reductions
no word-operation counter in the module

kernels.measure: derive from matrix shape (rows x words x pivots / 2) and pass --ops, labelled derived
kernels.note: Finding: dense F_2 elimination has no counter; the F4 path that calls similar code does.

ops_counter.what: products and sparse_products (matrix-vector products), row_ops; not the nonzeros multiplied

kernels.measure: ops = sparse_products x nnz, both from the stage output, passed with --ops
kernels.note: Counter is one level too coarse: a product's cost is nnz mulmods. Emit nnz x products.

ops_counter.what: no operation counter

kernels.note: Finding: block Wiedemann reports no matvec or mulmod count.

ops_counter.what: krylov_muls, bm_muls, nf_muls, readout_muls, roots_muls
no counter; the bench performs a fixed number of multiplications per iteration

kernels.note: Needs an IFMA host (avx512ifma is present on the authoring host). v1 has no 52-bit IFMA class; mulwide_u64 is the nearest ceiling.

ops_counter.what: --bench prints scalar updates per second and total updates

kernels.measure: prefer ecc2k130/roofline.py and cryptanalysis/gpueff for this kernel; optlevel gpu measure --ops-regex 'updates[=: ]+(\d+)' -- ./ecc2k130 --curve 131 --bench ...
kernels.note: Already has a per-pipe roofline (ROOFLINE.md: 0.73 of the carry-less speed of light at 20 B/s). The bound is the CLMAD pipe, which v1's classes do not model; do not re-score it more coarsely.

ops_counter.what: bench.cu reports steps per second

kernels.note: A step is many 32-bit multiply-adds; convert with the limb count or score as a lower bound.

ops_counter.what: none emitted; ops = nnz x products from the solve

kernels.note: Memory-roof kernel: declare 12-16 bytes per nonzero.

ops_counter.what: bench reports timings; multiply-adds follow from rows x columns x pivots
candidates enumerated (2^n); one Gray-code step is a few xors
polynomials processed; no multiplication counter
GroupOps.field_ops.muls+sqrs on the probe path (prepare excluded); IFMA path charges honest lane-Montgomery muls

kernels.note: Study dir research/rootfind_optlevel_20261121/. Attainment is not a speed claim. INTENSITY_UNKNOWN until bytes_declared is set.

ops_counter.what: group_ops and iterations per solve, printed by ca_perfbench

kernels.note: A group operation is several mulmods; same caveat as crypto.rho.prime_fast. Existing benchmarks: benchmarks/20261103-rho-zp-step, 20261101-rho-ec-step (cycles per step under perf).

kernels.path: src/linalg.c (dense row operations and threaded Lanczos mod q)

ops_counter.what: lanczos_iterations; no mulmod count

kernels.measure: ops = iterations x 2 x nnz, passed with --ops
kernels.note: Counter too coarse, as crypto.la.koblitz_sparse.

ops_counter.what: relations kept; no count of smoothness-test operations found

kernels.note: Finding.

ops_counter.what: iterations per launch x walkers

kernels.path: csd/ic_bounds_m3_batched.py, csd/ic_bounds_split_m.py (float64 exact products through numpy/OpenBLAS)

ops_counter.what: none in the engine; r*s*n per product follows from the shapes (research/optlevel_20261117/real_kernel/closure_wrapper.py counts it from outside)

kernels.measure: tools/optlevel/run.sh measure --scale env:OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS:1,4 --out M.json -- python3 research/optlevel_20261117/real_kernel/closure_wrapper.py /home/user/lfd-summation-systems OUT -- cell --m 4 --k 2 --primes 7681 --seeds 1
kernels.note: Finding: the engine reports seconds and batches but no operation count. The compiled echelon (csd/_elim.c) does count row operations and returns them; the callers drop the value.

kernels.path: csd/ic_bounds_big.py (numpy and CuPy backends sharing one path; matmul_sub, rref_block)

ops_counter.what: per-phase seconds (reduce, rref, update, h2d, d2h) and peak memory; no operation count

kernels.measure: optlevel gpu measure --ops <sum of r*s*n over matmul_sub calls> ... after adding the counter or wrapping matmul_sub as closure_wrapper.py does
kernels.note: Finding: the largest runs in the three repositories (k = 14, 499,178 columns) have phase timings but no operation count, so no attainment can be computed for them. The host/device transfer seconds are the host-idle-share analogue.

ops_counter.what: row operations in *ops (returned as the third value of elim.fp_echelon)

kernels.measure: call through a small driver and pass the returned count with --ops
kernels.note: A row operation is `cols` multiply-adds; multiply before scoring.
